result.topic_en: Riemann argues that the movements of the ear's sound-conducting apparatus are extremely small (beyond microscopic visibility) and that its solid parts must therefore fit exactly at their joints, and that little vibrational energy may be lost to other work before reaching the labyrinth.

items.english: If the tympanic apparatus is to transmit such small movements faithfully, as experience shows it does, then the solid bodies of which it consists must fit exactly onto one another at the places where they are to act on each other.

items.english: Furthermore, only a small part of the perceptible force of the sound motion may be lost to the labyrinth through other work, such as tensioning joint capsules and membranes.
